WOW. I already played the game, of which the game was based off the book, and they had very little in common beyond a few names and general setting. It is worth reading for any post apocalypse fans.

Background: the nuclear war was 20 years ago. The surface is so radioactive you cannot spend much time up there. Wired mutants and monsters roam and periodically sneak into the Moscow Metro, a giant mob shelter which is falling apart and affected by supernatural influences. Some areas try to stay civilized. Others fell to fanatical Nazism, Stalinism, satanism, and worse. The main character, Artyom, explores and gets dragged along to various places to try and save his home station.

This is very lord of the flies, and very, VERY Russian. It is atmospheric with tension and brief bursts of high impact action. No great battles but skirmishes that are very personal, with great lead up. Not a ton of character development but there are so many characters, excluding the main one, you get to know them long and well enough to miss them by the next chapter.

Definitely something to check out if you like slower, atmospheric and story driven apocalypse settings. I've seen gore threads on /b/ that were less dark than the latter half of this.
